home.title: How to compress a photo without ruining it
home.text1: Compression shrinks JPG, PNG and WebP files so they load faster on a website, fit form upload limits and do not clog your inbox. You stay in control of the result: a quality slider from 40 to 95%, set to 80% by default.
home.text2: By default the pixel dimensions stay the same. If you need a smaller image, untick the box and choose the long side: 3840, 2560, 1920 or 1280 px. Photos are compressed on your device and are not uploaded to a server.

benefits.title: Never heavier
benefits.text: If the compressed version is not smaller than the original, you get the original back.

benefits.title: Up to 20 photos at once
benefits.text: Each up to 30 MB. Download all results as a single ZIP.

benefits.title: Settings are remembered
benefits.text: Your chosen quality and size are kept for your next visit.

benefits.title: Any device
benefits.text: Windows, macOS, Android or iPhone — all you need is a browser.

faq.q: Why does a PNG barely shrink?
faq.a: PNG stores pixels losslessly, so the quality slider has little effect on it. Reduce the long side or convert the file to WebP or JPG instead.

faq.q: Which quality should I choose?
faq.a: Start at 80%. If the file is still too large, lower the quality or limit the resolution, then compare the result with the original.

faq.q: How do I compress a photo to an exact number of KB?
faq.a: Use “Compress to a Size”: you enter the target and the tool picks the quality for you.

faq.q: Can I compress HEIC photos from an iPhone?
faq.a: Not on this page, which accepts JPG, PNG and WebP. Convert iPhone photos to JPG first.

convert.title: JPG converter: when you need one
convert.text1: Almost every website, form, messenger and older program accepts JPG. So a PNG, WebP or iPhone HEIC picture is often easier to convert than to find something that opens it.
convert.text2: The converter saves results at 90% quality. Transparent areas are filled with white, because the format has no transparency. Add up to 20 files of 30 MB each and download them together as one archive.

benefits.title: iPhone photos
benefits.text: HEIC and HEIF files convert right on the page, with no extra software.

benefits.title: White instead of black
benefits.text: A transparent background will not turn black: the tool puts white underneath.

benefits.title: Batch processing
benefits.text: Several files at once, all results in one ZIP.

benefits.title: Done on your device
benefits.text: Files are converted in your browser rather than on a server.

faq.q: Which formats can be converted?
faq.a: PNG, WebP, BMP, HEIC and HEIF.

faq.q: Why did my transparent PNG get a white background?
faq.a: JPG cannot store transparency. To keep those areas from turning black, the converter fills them with white. If you need transparency, use “Convert to PNG”.

faq.q: What quality is the result?
faq.a: 90%. Compression artifacts are usually invisible at this level, while the file stays a reasonable size.

resize.title: Resize a photo for a website or social media
resize.text1: Phone photos are often bigger than needed: a website form asks for specific dimensions, and a social network crops the image its own way. Here you can set an exact width and height or use a ready-made preset.
resize.text2: Presets: Instagram 1080×1080, Facebook 1200×630, YouTube 1280×720, Twitter 1600×900. When the proportions change, you drag the frame yourself and choose which part of the shot to keep.

benefits.title: Proportions under control
benefits.text: With aspect ratio locked, type the width and the height is calculated for you.

benefits.title: Your framing
benefits.text: Drag the crop area to decide what stays in the picture.

benefits.title: Three formats
benefits.text: Save the result as JPG, PNG or WebP.

benefits.title: White background for JPG
benefits.text: A transparent PNG saved as JPG gets white, not black, behind it.

faq.q: Can I change only the width?
faq.a: Yes. While the aspect ratio is locked, the height is calculated automatically.

faq.q: What if I set different proportions?
faq.a: The extra part is cropped. Use the frame on the preview to choose which part of the photo stays.

faq.q: How do I reduce the file size rather than the pixels?
faq.a: Use the compressor on the home page or “Compress to a Size”: they reduce the size in kilobytes.

webp.title: Why convert photos to WebP
webp.text1: WebP is a Google image format that is usually a quarter to a third smaller than JPG at the same visual quality. On a website that means faster pages and better Core Web Vitals.
webp.text2: Here you can convert JPG, PNG, BMP and iPhone HEIC photos. Conversion runs in your browser, so your files are not sent anywhere.

benefits.title: Lighter pages
benefits.text: Smaller images speed up your site and use less of your visitors' mobile data.

benefits.title: Transparency kept
benefits.text: Logos and icons from PNG will not get a white background.

benefits.title: Up to 20 files at once
benefits.text: Up to 30 MB each, with all results in one ZIP.

benefits.title: Every browser reads it
benefits.text: Chrome, Firefox, Safari and Edge display the format with no setup.

faq.q: What quality does the converter use?
faq.a: 85%. At that level the picture looks almost like the original, while the file is noticeably lighter.

faq.q: Will older programs open WebP?
faq.a: Browsers show it, but some older viewers and editors do not. Keep a JPG copy for those.

faq.q: How much smaller will my file be?
faq.a: It depends on the picture: detailed photos shrink less, simple graphics shrink more. Compare the size before and after on your own file.

presets.title: What photo presets give you
presets.text1: A preset is a ready-made set of color, contrast and tone settings, like in Lightroom. You pick a style and it's applied to your photo, instead of adjusting every slider by hand.
presets.text2: More than 60 presets are grouped into 16 themed collections, from portrait and film looks to product shots and cars for sale. Using one style across all your photos makes a blog or shop feed recognizable.

benefits.title: Strength from 0 to 200%
benefits.text: The slider makes the effect barely visible or pushes it further.

benefits.title: Before/after view
benefits.text: A comparison slider shows the original and the result in one frame.

benefits.title: Collections for tasks
benefits.text: Brighten a dark shot, prepare a product photo, edit a wedding or profile picture.

benefits.title: Photo stays with you
benefits.text: Presets are applied in the browser and the file isn't sent anywhere.

faq.q: How do I pick the right preset?
faq.a: Start with a collection that matches your subject and compare a few options. Thumbnails are rendered from your own photo, so you see the real result.

faq.q: What about quality after editing?
faq.a: The photo is saved as a JPG at 92% quality with the long side up to 2000 px — plenty for social media and websites.

faq.q: Do I need Lightroom?
faq.a: No. Everything works on the site, and there are no preset files to download.

wordToPdf.title: Why save a Word document as PDF
wordToPdf.text1: A PDF looks the same on every device and in print: fonts, margins and tables stay in place. That's why résumés, contracts and business proposals are usually sent this way.
wordToPdf.text2: The conversion runs on a server: your file travels over an encrypted connection and is deleted from it automatically shortly afterwards. You don't need Word installed.

benefits.title: Layout unchanged
benefits.text: Fonts, tables, images and spacing carry over exactly as in the original.

benefits.title: Opens anywhere
benefits.text: The recipient only needs a browser or phone, not Word.

benefits.title: Up to 10 files at once
benefits.text: Several documents convert together and download as one archive.

benefits.title: Harder to change by accident
benefits.text: The recipient won't shift the layout or edit the text unintentionally.

faq.q: Which files can I convert?
faq.a: .doc and .docx up to 50 MB each, from any Word version or compatible editor.

faq.q: How many free conversions do I get?
faq.a: The daily number is limited. Registered users get a higher limit than guests.

faq.q: How do I make a PDF editable again?
faq.a: Use the separate PDF to Word converter — it produces a .docx you can edit.

pdfToWord.title: When to turn a PDF into Word
pdfToWord.text1: A PDF is easy to read and print but awkward to edit. Converting it to .docx lets you fix the text, tables and structure in Word or Google Docs without retyping.
pdfToWord.text2: It's a lifesaver when the original file is lost and all you have is the PDF of a contract, report or form. Processing happens on a server, and the file is deleted from it automatically shortly afterwards.

benefits.title: Editable .docx
benefits.text: The result opens right away in Word or Google Docs.

benefits.title: Document structure
benefits.text: Paragraphs, headings and basic formatting are carried over as closely as possible.

benefits.title: No retyping
benefits.text: There's no need to copy pages out by hand.

benefits.title: Several files at once
benefits.text: Up to 10 documents per batch, with all results in one archive.

faq.q: Do scanned PDFs work?
faq.a: PDFs with a text layer work best. For a scan, run image-to-text recognition first.

faq.q: Are tables and images kept?
faq.a: The basic structure carries over. A complex layout sometimes needs a manual touch-up.

faq.q: What are the limits?
faq.a: Up to 50 MB per file. Free conversions per day are limited, and registering raises the limit.

removeBg.title: Removing a photo background: when you need it
removeBg.text1: A transparent background is useful for marketplace product cards, profile pictures, slides and collages — anywhere the subject matters more than its surroundings. A neural network finds the outline on its own, so there's no tracing edges in Photoshop.
removeBg.text2: You can touch up the automatic result with the magic brush. Restore mode brings back parts erased by mistake, and Remove mode clears leftover background around hair or fine details. The file is saved as a PNG with transparency.

benefits.title: No manual outlining
benefits.text: The model separates a person, product or pet from the background by itself.

benefits.title: Brush touch-ups
benefits.text: Adjustable brush size lets you work precisely along tricky edges.

benefits.title: PNG with alpha
benefits.text: The cut-out sits on any banner or layout without a gray fringe.

benefits.title: No Photoshop needed
benefits.text: A browser on your computer or phone is enough.

faq.q: Does it work for product photos?
faq.a: Yes, that's one of the main uses — product cards for marketplaces and online stores.

faq.q: What if the background isn't removed cleanly?
faq.a: Open the magic brush: Restore brings back the areas you need, Remove erases what's left over.

faq.q: What format is the result?
faq.a: A PNG with a transparent background, meaning it has an alpha channel.

faq.q: Is my photo sent to a server?
faq.a: No. Your browser downloads the recognition model once, and after that the photo is processed on your device.

imageToText.title: Extract text from a photo, screenshot or scan
imageToText.text1: OCR turns a picture of a page into plain text you can copy and edit. No more retyping a quote from a book, a contract clause or a presentation slide.
imageToText.text2: Before uploading, pick the document's languages: Ukrainian, Russian, English or Spanish, up to three at once. Choosing the right language matters most for accuracy. Save the result as .txt or .doc.

benefits.title: Up to 20 images at once
benefits.text: Each file is recognized separately, and you can download all results together.

benefits.title: Mixed-language documents
benefits.text: For example, Ukrainian with English terms in a manual or contract.

benefits.title: Snap with your camera
benefits.text: On a phone you can photograph the page directly instead of picking a file.

benefits.title: Stays on your device
benefits.text: Recognition runs locally, so confidential papers never leave your computer.

faq.q: Which files can I use?
faq.a: JPG, PNG, WebP and BMP up to 15 MB: screenshots, photos of documents, scans.

faq.q: Can it read handwriting?
faq.a: It works best with printed type. Handwriting comes out with noticeable errors.

faq.q: Why did I get gibberish instead of words?
faq.a: Most likely the document's language isn't selected. Add it in the language picker and run recognition again.

faq.q: Which format should I save?
faq.a: .txt for plain text, .doc to open the result straight in Word.

compressToSize.title: How to compress a photo to a target size in KB
compressToSize.text1: Government portals, job applications, email and classifieds sites often set a cap like 200 KB per photo. Regular compression is guesswork here: you never know how big the file will end up. This tool works the other way round. You set the limit, and it picks the quality and, if needed, the resolution.
compressToSize.text2: For every file you see the size before and after, the quality used and the final resolution. The result is saved as JPEG or WebP.

benefits.title: A limit in KB or MB
benefits.text: Pick 50, 100, 200, 500 or 1000 KB, or type your own number. The file will not go over it.

benefits.title: Best quality that fits
benefits.text: The tool doesn't shrink files just to be safe. It looks for the highest quality that still fits.

benefits.title: Scans stay with you
benefits.text: Compression runs on your device, so ID scans and application photos are never uploaded.

benefits.title: Up to 20 photos at once
benefits.text: One limit for the whole batch, and several results download as a single ZIP file.

sections.title: How the size is found
sections.text: The tool first tries 95% quality. If the file is too big, it runs a binary search between 95% and 30%, with eight attempts at most. When even 30% is not enough, it scales the image down in 85% steps. It never goes below 600 pixels on the long side. One kilobyte here means 1000 bytes, so the file passes any site's size check.

sections.title: JPEG or WebP
sections.text: Almost every site and form accepts JPEG. WebP is usually smaller at the same quality, but older systems can't open it. If you're not sure a form takes WebP, choose JPEG.

sections.title: Limitations
sections.text: A very small limit on a detailed photo means a visible loss of sharpness. If the target can't be reached even at 600 pixels, you'll see the smallest size achieved instead of a ruined file. Transparent PNG areas turn white. Capture date, location and the color profile are not kept. Each file can be up to 30 MB.

faq.q: How do I reduce a photo to 200 KB?
faq.a: Pick 200 KB, add your photo and download the result. The tool chooses the quality and, if needed, the resolution for you.

faq.q: Can I compress a photo to 100 KB without losing quality?
faq.a: Not entirely, because JPEG and WebP are lossy formats. On simple images the difference is barely visible. Detailed shots under a small limit will show artifacts.

faq.q: What if my photo is already under the limit?
faq.a: A JPG, PNG or WebP that already fits is returned unchanged. Compressing it again would only lower the quality.

faq.q: Does it work with iPhone HEIC photos?
faq.a: Yes, HEIC is converted to JPEG or WebP. The extra module for this only loads when you add a HEIC file.

convertToPng.title: When to convert an image to PNG
convertToPng.text1: PNG keeps every pixel without loss and supports real transparency. It's what people ask for with logos, screenshots, diagrams and design mockups. Yet images often arrive in other formats: WebP saved from a browser, HEIC from an iPhone, AVIF or GIF. This page turns them into a file that opens anywhere.
convertToPng.text2: The pixel dimensions stay the same, and the orientation stored by your phone is respected. You can convert several files together and get them as one ZIP.

benefits.title: Transparency is kept
benefits.text: Transparent areas from WebP, AVIF or GIF don't turn black or white.

benefits.title: No sideways photos
benefits.text: The rotation your camera wrote into the file is applied automatically.

benefits.title: Seven input formats
benefits.text: JPG, WebP, BMP, GIF, AVIF, HEIC and HEIF, up to 20 files at a time.

benefits.title: Work files stay offline
benefits.text: Conversion runs on your device, so mockups and screenshots are never sent anywhere.

sections.title: How a lossless format differs from JPG
sections.text: Lossless images shine where there is crisp text, sharp edges or a transparent background. Regular photos get heavier than in JPG or WebP because of smooth color gradients. If file size matters for email or a website, stay with JPG or WebP. Converting won't remove artifacts already present in a JPG. But from now on you can edit and re-save the file without further loss.

sections.title: What happens to transparency
sections.text: Transparent areas from WebP, AVIF and GIF carry over as they are. JPG and BMP have no transparency, so their background stays colored. Making it transparent takes a separate background removal step.

sections.title: Limitations
sections.text: Only the first frame of an animated GIF or WebP is kept. EXIF data and GPS coordinates are not copied. A converted HEIC photo can become very large. The limit is 30 MB per file. AVIF only opens if your browser supports it.

faq.q: Will the file get smaller?
faq.a: Usually not, since lossless photos weigh more. To reduce the size, use compression instead.

faq.q: Will the background become transparent after converting a JPG?
faq.a: No, the background color stays. Only background removal makes it transparent.

faq.q: Is quality lost?
faq.a: The conversion itself loses nothing, as the pixels are copied exactly. Any loss already in a JPG or WebP remains.

faq.q: What happens to a GIF animation?
faq.a: Only the first frame is saved as a still image.

removeExif.title: Remove EXIF and GPS data from a photo before sharing
removeExif.text1: A phone photo stores the camera model, the date and time, sometimes a serial number, the author and the editing app. The most sensitive part is GPS: it shows where the picture was taken, including your home.
removeExif.text2: This page shows what each file contains and strips it out. For JPEG, PNG and WebP the pixels are not re-encoded, so quality stays the same. Cleaned files get “-clean” added to their names.

benefits.title: See what was inside
benefits.text: Camera, date, software, author, serial number and a separate warning about coordinates.

benefits.title: The image is not re-saved
benefits.text: Only metadata blocks are cut out; the image data keeps the exact same bytes.

benefits.title: Coordinates stay on your device
benefits.text: Your browser reads and removes the metadata, and files are not sent anywhere.

benefits.title: Up to 20 photos at once
benefits.text: JPEG, PNG and WebP up to 30 MB each; several results download as one ZIP.

sections.title: What exactly is removed
sections.text: From JPEG: EXIF with camera, date, settings, GPS and thumbnail, plus XMP, IPTC, comments and data after the image ends. From PNG: text fields, EXIF and modification time; from WebP: EXIF and XMP. The ICC color profile stays, so colors do not shift.

sections.title: Why quality does not change
sections.text: The usual way to “clean” a photo is to open and re-save it, which degrades a JPEG each time. Here the metadata blocks are cut out and the compressed image data is copied unchanged. Pixels before and after match exactly.

sections.title: The rotation tag and full re-encoding
sections.text: Portrait phone photos are often stored sideways and displayed correctly thanks to a rotation tag. So in JPEG this tag is kept; it contains nothing personal. To remove everything, turn on full re-encoding. The photo is physically rotated, but JPEG and WebP are re-saved at 92% quality and the color profile becomes standard sRGB.

sections.title: Limitations
sections.text: A clean file does not make a photo anonymous: faces, signs and license plates stay in the picture. HEIC is not supported, so convert it to JPG first. Extra frames such as an HDR map are removed too, so on an HDR screen the photo may look a little different. Animated PNG and WebP are cleaned only without re-encoding.

faq.q: Can removed metadata be restored?
faq.a: Not from the cleaned file — the blocks are physically gone. If you may need the data, keep the original separately.

faq.q: Don't social networks strip EXIF themselves?
faq.a: Some do when you publish, but not all and not always. When a photo is sent as a file, by email or to cloud storage, the data usually stays.

faq.q: How can I check that GPS is really gone?
faq.a: After processing, each file shows a summary of what was found and removed, plus its size before and after.

faq.q: How do I clean an iPhone photo?
faq.a: Save or convert it to JPG first, then add it here. This page does not accept HEIC.

photoToPdf.title: How to combine several photos into one PDF
photoToPdf.text1: One PDF is easier to send than a dozen separate photos: the pages stay in order and don't get lost in a chat. People use it for document scans, notebook pages, receipts for an expense report or product photos for a catalog. Many portals accept only one file, and a PDF solves that.
photoToPdf.text2: Add your photos, put them in order and choose the page size and margins. The document is built on your device, so your scans are never sent anywhere.

benefits.title: Your page order
benefits.text: Use the ↑↓ arrows or drag and drop to arrange the photos the way they should appear.

benefits.title: JPEG and PNG not re-encoded
benefits.text: Plain JPEGs without a rotation tag and PNGs are embedded as they are, with no extra compression.

benefits.title: A4 or photo size
benefits.text: An A4 sheet with margins for printing, or a page that matches the photo exactly.

benefits.title: Even a single photo
benefits.text: One image gives a one-page document, handy for sending a scan.

sections.title: A4 or photo size
sections.text: On A4, each photo is fitted to the sheet without changing its proportions. Portrait or landscape orientation is chosen automatically from the shape of the shot. The photo-size mode makes the page exactly as large as the image, with no white bars. A 10 mm margin adds space on every side, which helps for printing or binding.

sections.title: What happens to quality
sections.text: JPEGs without a rotation tag and plain PNGs go into the document unchanged. Portrait shots from a phone with a rotation tag, plus WebP, BMP, GIF, AVIF and HEIC, are first turned the right way up. They are then re-encoded as JPEG at 92% quality, and transparent areas become white.

sections.title: Limitations
sections.text: Up to 20 photos at a time, each up to 30 MB. If they add up to more than 200 MB, you'll see a warning, but the file is still created. On slower devices a large album takes longer. The tool doesn't add page numbers, captions or watermarks.

faq.q: Can I change the photo order after adding them?
faq.a: Yes, until you create the PDF: use the ↑↓ arrows next to each file or drag it in the list.

faq.q: Will the photos lose quality in the PDF?
faq.a: JPEGs and PNGs without rotation are embedded unchanged. Other images are re-encoded as JPEG at 92% quality to keep the correct orientation.

faq.q: Which page size should I choose?
faq.a: A4 for printing and official documents. Photo size when you want the original proportions with no white margins.

faq.q: How many photos can I combine?
faq.a: Up to 20 files at a time, up to 30 MB each.

cropImage.title: Crop a photo online to the right aspect ratio
cropImage.text1: Cropping removes clutter from the edges and fits a photo to where it will be posted. A profile picture needs a square, Stories and Reels need a 9:16 vertical frame, and a video cover needs 16:9.
cropImage.text2: Drag the crop box with a mouse or a finger, or pull its corners. When a ratio is locked, the box keeps its shape even while you resize it from a corner.

benefits.title: Exact pixel sizes
benefits.text: The original and selection sizes are shown next to the preview.

benefits.title: Works on touchscreens
benefits.text: The box and its corners are easy to drag on a phone or tablet.

benefits.title: Nothing is uploaded
benefits.text: Cropping happens on your device. The image is never sent to a server.

sections.title: Which ratio to choose
sections.text: 1:1 suits avatars and square posts. 4:3 and 3:2 are classic photo frames, and 3:4 and 2:3 are their vertical versions. 16:9 fits covers and banners, 9:16 fits Stories. If none of these works, pick “Free”.

sections.title: How the crop box behaves
sections.text: Drag the middle of the box to move the selection. Drag a corner to resize it while the opposite corner stays put. The box can't leave the photo.

sections.title: Quality and output format
sections.text: Pixels inside the box are not changed. JPG and WebP are saved at 92% quality, and PNG is saved without lossy compression. Transparent areas turn white in JPG.

faq.q: Can I crop a photo into a circle?
faq.a: The crop box here is rectangular. For a round avatar with transparent corners, use the separate “Circle Crop Photo” tool.

faq.q: How do I make a square profile picture?
faq.a: Choose 1:1, move the box over the face and resize it from a corner. It stays square.

faq.q: Can I crop several photos at once?
faq.a: No, the tool works with one photo. After downloading the result, you can open the next one right away.

faq.q: Will the file get smaller after cropping?
faq.a: Usually yes, since fewer pixels remain. If you need a specific file size, use “Compress to a Size” after cropping.

rotateImage.title: Rotate or flip a photo online
rotateImage.text1: Phone photos sometimes open sideways or upside down. The camera misread the orientation, or the viewer ignores the rotation tag. Here you can turn the image by 90°, 180° or 270° and mirror it if needed.
rotateImage.text2: Flipping solves different problems. Text in a mirror selfie reads backwards. A face on a portrait should look toward the copy on a layout. You can combine both actions, and the preview changes after every click.

benefits.title: A quarter turn per click
benefits.text: Use “Left 90°” or “Right 90°”. Two clicks in a row give you 180°.

benefits.title: Flip on either axis
benefits.text: Horizontal flip swaps left and right. Vertical flip swaps top and bottom.

benefits.title: No resampling
benefits.text: Turns in 90° steps only move pixels around, so sharpness stays the same.

benefits.title: The file stays with you
benefits.text: Rotation runs in your browser tab. The site never receives or stores your photo.

sections.title: Rotating and flipping together
sections.text: Order doesn't matter: flip first and rotate later, or the other way round. Click a button again to undo it. The result size is shown under the preview; after a 90° turn, width and height swap.

sections.title: When quality can still drop
sections.text: Rotation itself loses nothing. A small loss can happen only when saving as JPG or WebP, because both formats compress. Save as PNG if you need an exact copy of the pixels.

sections.title: Transparent backgrounds
sections.text: PNG and WebP keep the original transparency. JPG has no transparency, so those areas are filled with white rather than black.

faq.q: Can I rotate by a custom angle, like 15°?
faq.a: No, only 90° steps and flips are available. This tool won't straighten a tilted horizon.

faq.q: What's the difference between rotating and flipping?
faq.a: Rotating turns the frame around its center. Flipping creates a mirror image along one axis without turning it.

faq.q: Why does my iPhone photo open rotated?
faq.a: Cameras often store orientation in a separate tag, and some apps ignore it. Rotating here bakes the orientation into the pixels.

faq.q: Which files can I rotate?
faq.a: JPEG, PNG, WebP, BMP, GIF, AVIF and HEIC up to 30 MB. You can save as JPG, PNG or WebP.

addWatermark.title: How to add a watermark to a photo
addWatermark.text1: A watermark shows who took the photo and makes unauthorized reuse harder. Photographers sign their portfolios, sellers put a logo on product shots, and bloggers brand their screenshots.
addWatermark.text2: The watermark can be text or your own logo. Place it in a corner, in the center, or repeat it as a tile across the whole frame. Every change shows up in the preview immediately.

benefits.title: Text or logo
benefits.text: Type a signature or upload a logo file. Position and opacity work the same for both.

benefits.title: Tile mode
benefits.text: The mark repeats across the whole photo, so it can't simply be cropped out.

benefits.title: Size in percent
benefits.text: The mark scales with the photo and looks the same on small and large images.

benefits.title: Your logo stays local
benefits.text: Both the photo and the logo file are processed in your browser tab.

sections.title: Text mark or logo
sections.text: Text is enough for a name, studio name or website address. You can pick the color and a font size from 2 to 15% of the photo. For a logo, a PNG with a transparent background works best: there's no white box around the mark.

sections.title: Position: corner, center or tile
sections.text: A corner mark barely gets in the way, but it's easy to crop off. The center is more visible. Tile mode protects best because the text covers the whole frame, though it's more noticeable.

sections.title: Opacity
sections.text: The slider sets opacity from 5% to 100%. Around 20–40% the mark is visible without hiding details. At 5% it's barely noticeable but still part of the file.

faq.q: How do I make the watermark semi-transparent?
faq.a: Lower the opacity with the slider. The minimum is 5%.

faq.q: Why is there a white box around my logo?
faq.a: Your logo is probably a JPG without transparency. Use a PNG with a transparent background.

faq.q: Can I watermark several photos at once?
faq.a: No, the mark is applied to one photo at a time. For a series, repeat the same settings for each image.

faq.q: Which files can I use?
faq.a: Photos and logos in JPEG, PNG, WebP, BMP, GIF, AVIF or HEIC, photos up to 30 MB. The result is JPG, PNG or WebP.

blackAndWhite.title: Black and white photo online with adjustable strength
blackAndWhite.text1: Without color, a photo is reduced to shape, light and shadow. That is why a black and white version often looks stronger than the original. It also rescues shots with mixed lighting, where daylight and a yellow lamp produce muddy tones.
blackAndWhite.text2: Upload a photo and move the slider from 0 to 100%. The preview follows the slider, so there is no separate “Apply” step. The result is saved as JPG, PNG or WebP with “-bw” added to the file name.

benefits.title: Strength you choose
benefits.text: The slider is smooth: tone colors down slightly or remove them completely.

benefits.title: See it as you drag
benefits.text: The preview redraws while the slider moves, so the right balance is easy to judge by eye.

benefits.title: Detail stays intact
benefits.text: Only pixel colors change; their position and the sharpness of the image are untouched.

benefits.title: The photo stays on your device
benefits.text: Your browser does the conversion, and the site never receives a copy.

sections.title: Partial desaturation instead of an on/off switch
sections.text: At 100% you get a classic black and white photo. At 40–60% colors remain but become calmer. This suits portraits and shots with a loud background, where removing all color takes away too much.

sections.title: How the gray tone is calculated
sections.text: Each pixel's brightness uses the standard weights: red 0.299, green 0.587, blue 0.114. Television uses the same coefficients for a monochrome signal. As a result, foliage does not sink into black and the sky does not turn into a white patch.

sections.title: When black and white works best
sections.text: Portrait photographers use it to hide uneven skin tone or a poor white balance. Designers use it to unify a series shot on different cameras. On a résumé or an official document, a monochrome photo looks restrained.

faq.q: How is this different from sepia?
faq.a: This tool produces shades of gray based on brightness. Sepia adds a warm brown tone; you will find it among the film presets.

faq.q: Will my original file change?
faq.a: No. You download a new file with “-bw” in its name, and the original stays as it was.

faq.q: What happens to a transparent PNG?
faq.a: PNG and WebP keep the transparency. JPG cannot store it, so empty areas become white.

faq.q: Can I convert an iPhone photo in HEIC?
faq.a: Yes. HEIC opens just like JPEG, PNG, WebP, BMP, GIF or AVIF.

circleCrop.title: Circle crop for profile pictures and logos
circleCrop.text1: Social networks and messengers show profile photos as circles. Upload a rectangular picture and the platform crops it for you, often cutting off part of a face or a logo. Cropping the circle yourself means the frame contains exactly what you want.
circleCrop.text2: The frame here always stays a circle, whatever the proportions of the original. Move it over a face or an object and resize it with the corner handles. The result is saved as PNG, WebP or JPG.

benefits.title: A circle, never an oval
benefits.text: However you drag the handles, the frame keeps its round shape.

benefits.title: Transparent corners
benefits.text: In PNG and WebP everything outside the circle is transparent, so the avatar sits on any background.

benefits.title: Pixels are not resampled
benefits.text: The circle's content is copied from the original as is; compression only happens when saving to JPG or WebP.

benefits.title: Works with a finger too
benefits.text: On a phone you move the frame by touch, just as you would with a mouse.

sections.title: Where a round photo is needed
sections.text: Avatars on Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, Telegram, Discord and WhatsApp. Profile photos for Zoom and Google Meet. Round logos, badges and community icons.

sections.title: How to cut out a circle
steps: Open a photo — a round frame appears in the center.
Drag the frame over the area you need and set its size with a corner handle.
Pick a format and click “Crop and download”.

sections.title: PNG or JPG for a round photo
sections.text: PNG is the default: the corners outside the circle are transparent and no quality is lost. WebP is transparent too but lighter. JPG has no transparency, so the corners are filled with white — fine for a white background or for print.

faq.q: Can I crop an oval?
faq.a: No, the frame is always round. For a rectangle or custom proportions, use the “Crop image” tool.

faq.q: Why crop it myself if the network shows a circle anyway?
faq.a: You decide what ends up in the center. Transparent corners also matter for a logo on a website or in a presentation.

faq.q: Can anyone see my photo?
faq.a: No. The browser crops it on a canvas, and the file is not sent to a server.

faq.q: What will the finished file be called?
faq.a: “-circle” is added to the original name, for example photo-circle.png.

compressVideo.title: How to compress a video online without ruining the picture
compressVideo.text1: A phone video can easily weigh hundreds of megabytes. Messengers and email either reject a file like that or squeeze it themselves, often badly. Here you shrink it in advance and decide how far to go.
compressVideo.text2: “Recommended” scales the frame down to 720p when the original is larger, which is enough for messengers and social media. With “Custom size” you enter the file size you want in megabytes, and the resolution is chosen to match. The output is always MP4 with H.264.

benefits.title: Target size in MB
benefits.text: Know the platform's upload limit? Type it in and the tool works out the resolution needed.

benefits.title: Settings per file
benefits.text: Add up to 5 videos and pick a mode for each one. A target larger than the file is flagged right away.

benefits.title: No upscaling
benefits.text: Resolution is never increased, since that would only bloat the file without adding detail.

benefits.title: MP4, MOV, AVI, WebM, MKV
benefits.text: Common formats from phones, cameras and screen recorders are accepted, up to 200 MB each.

sections.title: Why the size in MB is approximate
sections.text: The tool doesn't control bitrate directly. It estimates which resolution to request so the file lands near your target. Fast-moving scenes compress worse than static ones, so the result can differ a little. You see both the target and the actual size under the file.

sections.title: What happens to quality
sections.text: Most of the saving comes from fewer pixels per frame. The aspect ratio is kept, so nothing gets stretched. On a phone screen 720p looks clean, but for professional editing keep working from the original.

sections.title: Where the video is processed
sections.text: Unlike the photo editors on this site, video isn't re-encoded in your browser. A browser can't handle that much work, so a processing service does it. The file goes there only for the job. compressphoto.org doesn't keep it, and the service deletes it afterwards.

faq.q: What if I enter a size larger than the file itself?
faq.a: The “Compress” button stays disabled and a note explains why. The target has to be smaller than the original.

faq.q: Is the sound kept?
faq.a: Yes. Only the video track is changed; the audio stays as it was.

faq.q: What format will I get back?
faq.a: Always MP4 with H.264, which plays on virtually any phone, browser or player.

faq.q: Why does a video take longer than a photo?
faq.a: Re-encoding video is heavy work, and the upload adds time on top. A large clip can take a minute or more.

faq.q: How many compressions per day are free?
faq.a: There is a daily limit. Registered users get a higher one than guests.

convertMovToMp4.title: MOV to MP4: iPhone videos that open anywhere
convertMovToMp4.text1: iPhones, iPads and Apple cameras record video as MOV (QuickTime). Outside Apple's world such files sometimes refuse to open. Older Windows Media Player asks for codecs, some Android editors can't see them, and upload forms on websites turn them down.
convertMovToMp4.text2: This MOV to MP4 converter re-encodes the video to H.264, the combination nearly everything can play. How much the file changes depends on your camera settings. A clip already in H.264 is mostly just repackaged. Video shot in “High Efficiency” (HEVC, H.265) is fully re-encoded.

benefits.title: iPhone HEVC works too
benefits.text: “High Efficiency” clips become H.264 and open on devices that don't support HEVC.

benefits.title: Minimal change for H.264
benefits.text: If the MOV is already H.264, mostly the container changes and quality barely moves.

benefits.title: Several clips at once
benefits.text: Add up to 5 files from your gallery, each up to 200 MB.

benefits.title: Resolution untouched
benefits.text: The frame keeps its size. To make the file smaller, use “Compress video”.

sections.title: Where MOV usually gets rejected
sections.text: Modern Macs and Windows open MOV; the trouble is everything around them. Corporate upload systems, some messengers and older editing apps can throw a format error. MP4 is accepted almost everywhere, so converting first settles the question wherever the file goes next.

sections.title: Will quality drop?
sections.text: For H.264 the difference is minimal. HEVC is fully re-encoded, otherwise the file wouldn't open on devices without that codec. The picture stays good, but it isn't a bit-for-bit copy.

sections.title: Limits
sections.text: Up to 200 MB per file. Free conversions per day are limited, and registered users get more.

faq.q: Where does my iPhone video go?
faq.a: To a processing service, because a browser can't re-encode a video stream on its own. The file is sent there only for the conversion and deleted afterwards; compressphoto.org doesn't store it.

faq.q: Is the audio kept?
faq.a: Yes, only the video stream and the container change.

faq.q: How is this different from “Compress video”?
faq.a: Compression lowers the resolution to cut the file size. This page only switches the format to MP4 with H.264 and leaves the frame size alone.

faq.q: Can I upload MKV or WebM here?
faq.a: No, this page takes .mov files only. MKV and WebM have their own converters, and “Compress video” accepts five formats.

convertMkvToMp4.title: MKV to MP4: so your TV and phone can play the movie
convertMkvToMp4.text1: MKV (Matroska) is an open container used for movie rips and recordings with several audio tracks or subtitles. That flexibility is exactly why smart TVs, iPhones, game consoles and some editors refuse MKV or show a black screen.
convertMkvToMp4.text2: This MKV to MP4 converter re-encodes the video to H.264 and carries over the main audio track. MP4 with H.264 plays on almost every player and TV, whatever codec the original used.

benefits.title: Any codec inside
benefits.text: HEVC, VP9 or old DivX/Xvid — the output is always H.264.

benefits.title: Main audio stays
benefits.text: The primary audio track moves into the MP4 along with the video.

benefits.title: For TVs, consoles and editing
benefits.text: The result opens where the MKV gave a format error.

benefits.title: A few episodes at once
benefits.text: Add up to 5 files, each up to 200 MB.

sections.title: Why an MKV shows a black screen
sections.text: MKV is just an envelope. The video inside may be HEVC, VP9 or DivX/Xvid, and the sound DTS, AC3 or FLAC. A device has to support every one of those codecs. If even one is missing, you lose the picture or the sound.

sections.title: What doesn't carry over
sections.text: The output gets the main audio track. Extra tracks and subtitles embedded in the MKV aren't moved to MP4 automatically. If you need a different dub, check the file after converting.

sections.title: Re-encoding and limits
sections.text: MKV almost always holds codecs MP4 can't take directly, so the video is fully re-encoded. Quality stays good, though it isn't an exact copy. A processing service does the work and deletes the file afterwards. The limit is 200 MB per file.

faq.q: Why won't my MKV play on the TV?
faq.a: Most likely the TV doesn't support a codec inside the file, such as HEVC or VP9. After conversion to MP4 with H.264 the problem goes away.

faq.q: Can I shrink the file at the same time?
faq.a: No, this tool leaves the resolution alone because its job is compatibility. To get a lighter file, use “Compress video”.

faq.q: Can I convert several episodes at once?
faq.a: Yes, up to 5 files per batch. Each one must be 200 MB or less.

faq.q: How many free conversions do I get per day?
faq.a: The daily number is limited. Registered users have a higher limit than guests.

convertWebmToMp4.title: WebM to MP4: screen recordings for slides and editors
convertWebmToMp4.text1: WebM, built on the VP8/VP9 codecs, is a format made for the web. Browser screen recorders, webcams and screencast services save clips in it. The trouble starts when you need the recording in PowerPoint or Keynote, or in iMovie, an older Premiere or Vegas.
convertWebmToMp4.text2: Those apps expect H.264 and simply don't recognize VP8/VP9. This WebM to MP4 converter re-encodes the video to H.264 and keeps the sound. After that, presentations, editors and platforms without WebM support accept the file.

benefits.title: Drops into presentations
benefits.text: PowerPoint and Keynote take MP4 with H.264 without extra codecs.

benefits.title: Ready for editing
benefits.text: Open the screen recording straight away in a classic video editor.

benefits.title: Long recordings up to 200 MB
benefits.text: A screencast several minutes long usually fits within that limit.

benefits.title: Audio track preserved
benefits.text: Only the video is re-encoded; voice and music stay.

sections.title: Why WebM won't open outside the browser
sections.text: Browsers handle WebM well because it was designed for the web. Desktop apps and older devices often know only H.264/MP4. To them VP8/VP9 is an unknown codec, so the file won't open.

sections.title: Quality after re-encoding
sections.text: VP8/VP9 and H.264 are fundamentally different codecs, so simple repackaging isn't possible. The video is fully re-encoded: it still looks good but isn't identical to the original.

sections.title: Limits
sections.text: For high-resolution screen recordings, keep the 200 MB limit in mind before you start. Free conversions per day are limited, and signing up gives you more.

faq.q: Why won't PowerPoint insert my WebM?
faq.a: PowerPoint and Keynote don't recognize VP8/VP9, the codecs WebM is built on. The converted MP4 inserts without trouble.

faq.q: Will my recording stay on a server?
faq.a: No. A processing service does the re-encoding, since a browser can't. The recording is there only during conversion and is deleted afterwards; compressphoto.org doesn't keep it.

faq.q: Does the resolution change?
faq.a: No, the frame size stays the same. If you need a lighter file, the “Compress video” tool lowers the resolution.

faq.q: Can I convert several recordings at once?
faq.a: Yes, up to 5 files per batch, each up to 200 MB.

videoToMp3.title: Video to MP3 online: keep just the audio
videoToMp3.text1: Sometimes you only need the sound from a video. It might be a song from a music video, a recorded lecture or a podcast for your walk. An MP3 is many times smaller than the video and plays anywhere, from your phone to your car stereo.
videoToMp3.text2: The tool takes the first audio track and encodes it to MP3 at 128, 192 or 320 kbps. The work is done by FFmpeg, which your browser loads from our domain as a WebAssembly module. The video itself stays on your computer or phone.

benefits.title: No daily limits
benefits.text: Your device does the converting, not our server. So there is no queue and no cap on files per day.

benefits.title: Up to 10 files at once
benefits.text: Each up to 1000 MB. Several finished MP3s download together as one ZIP.

benefits.title: Three quality levels
benefits.text: 128, 192 or 320 kbps. The site remembers your choice for next time.

benefits.title: Works on phones
benefits.text: Pick a video from your iPhone or Android gallery and save the MP3 without installing an app.

sections.title: Which bitrate to pick
sections.text: Bitrate is how much data goes into each second of sound. 128 kbps is about 1 MB per minute and is plenty for speech. 192 kbps (about 1.4 MB per minute) suits music and most videos. 320 kbps (about 2.4 MB per minute) is the MP3 maximum and makes sense for good headphones. A higher bitrate cannot make the sound better than it was in the video.

sections.title: Limitations
sections.text: Speed depends on your device, so an old phone takes noticeably longer than a laptop. Only the first audio track is kept, which means a multi-language film gives you the main language. If the video has no sound, the tool tells you.

sections.title: When you only need part of it
sections.text: To save one song or quote from a long recording, cut it out first with “Trim Video”. Then turn that clip into an MP3 here.

faq.q: Which video formats work?
faq.a: MP4, MOV (including iPhone videos), WebM, MKV, AVI, M4V and 3GP. The file needs to contain an audio track.

faq.q: Why is the first conversion slower?
faq.a: Your browser downloads the processing engine once, about 30 MB. After that it comes from the cache and new files start right away.

faq.q: Does my video reach your server?
faq.a: No. Only FFmpeg is downloaded from us. Your browser reads the file from disk in chunks and processes it locally.

faq.q: Can I get lossless audio instead of MP3?
faq.a: Not yet. MP3 is the only output because every device opens it. At 192–320 kbps the difference from the original is hard to hear.

trimVideo.title: Trim video online: keep only the part you need
trimVideo.text1: Often a video does not need compressing, just shortening. Cut the dead time at both ends, grab a moment for a story, or send a colleague a few minutes of a meeting. A short clip also gets past messenger and email size limits more easily.
trimVideo.text2: Set the start and end with sliders, with the “Start here / End here” buttons or by typing exact times. You can preview the clip before saving. Trimming runs in your browser tab, and the file is not uploaded anywhere.

benefits.title: Original quality
benefits.text: Fast mode copies video and audio without re-encoding, so there is no blur and no artifacts.

benefits.title: Frame-accurate when needed
benefits.text: “Precise trim” cuts exactly at the times you set and saves the clip as a widely compatible MP4.

benefits.title: Your recordings stay yours
benefits.text: We never see the video or even its name, because it never reaches our server.

benefits.title: Big files
benefits.text: Up to 1000 MB per video and up to three videos at a time, with no daily limit.

sections.title: Fast or precise trimming
sections.text: Video is stored as keyframes plus the changes between them. Fast mode cuts on keyframes and re-encodes nothing. The clip is ready in seconds and keeps its original format. The catch is that it may start a second or two early, or more in screen recordings. Precise mode re-encodes the clip to H.264 MP4 and cuts exactly where you said. It takes noticeably longer, because your browser does the encoding.

sections.title: If the preview does not show
sections.text: Some browsers cannot play certain formats, such as MKV or HEVC iPhone videos in Chrome on Windows. You can still trim them: the tool reads the duration, and you set the cut points with the sliders or exact times.

sections.title: If the clip is still too big
sections.text: When even the trimmed part exceeds a messenger limit, shrink it with “Compress Video”. To keep only the clip's sound, use “Video to MP3”.

faq.q: Why does my clip start a little earlier than I set?
faq.a: Fast mode cuts at the nearest keyframe so it does not have to re-encode. For frame-accurate cuts, turn on “Precise trim”.

faq.q: What format will the clip be?
faq.a: In fast mode it matches the original: MP4, MOV, WebM, MKV and so on. In precise mode it is always MP4 with H.264 video and AAC audio.

faq.q: Can I cut several clips from one video?
faq.a: One pass gives one clip. For another one, add the same video again and set new cut points.

faq.q: Can a phone handle a large file?
faq.a: In fast mode, yes. Precise mode may run out of memory on a phone with little RAM. In that case use fast mode or switch to a computer.

presetsPortrait.title: How to choose a portrait preset
presetsPortrait.text1: Skin and eyes matter most in a portrait. A good portrait preset is careful with orange and red tones, so faces don't turn yellow, pink or plastic-looking. For everyday shots and social media, start with the soft or natural-light presets. They lift the shadows slightly and add warmth, and the person still looks like themselves.
presetsPortrait.text2: Dramatic presets with deep shadows suit dark backgrounds, evening light and creative shots, while studio presets work for plain backdrops, business portraits and window light. You can reduce the strength of any preset with the slider: for portraits 50–70% is often enough for a noticeable but tasteful effect.

faq.q: Which preset should I use for a selfie or a phone photo?
faq.a: Start with “Natural Skin” or “Clean Minimal”: they even out light and skin tone without obvious stylization. If the photo is dark, raise the effect strength to 120–150%.

faq.q: Do presets change skin tone?
faq.a: Portrait presets adjust orange and red tones gently, but dramatic and retro styles can make skin cooler or warmer. Compare before/after with the slider and lower the strength if the tone looks unnatural.

faq.q: Can I show only soft or only studio presets?
faq.a: Yes. Above the list there's a style filter: Soft, Dramatic, Natural light and Studio. It keeps only the presets of the chosen style.

faq.q: Can I make a black and white portrait?
faq.a: Yes: the “Dramatic” filter includes a high-contrast black and white preset, and “Timeless B&W” gives a softer classic look. For a plain black and white conversion there is a separate “Black & White Photo” tool.

presetsNature.title: Landscape presets: what suits which light
presetsNature.text1: The same landscape looks completely different at noon, at sunset and on an overcast day. That's why the presets here are grouped by light and subject. “Golden hour” boosts warm orange tones and gently mutes blues. “Forest” works with greens, and the “Sea” presets add turquoise to water and sky without making it garish.
presetsNature.text2: The most common problem with outdoor photos is a gray sky and a flat image on a cloudy day. That's what the “Overcast” filter is for: its presets lift the shadows, add saturation and a touch of warmth so the shot stops looking dull. If the effect is too strong, reduce it with the slider — 70–100% is usually enough for landscapes.

faq.q: Which preset makes greenery more vivid?
faq.a: Try “Overcast Boost” or “Moody Green Vibe Preset” under the “Forest” or “Overcast” filter — they boost greens and yellows. For a more muted, film-like green, choose “Analog Green 200”.

faq.q: Will these presets work with phone photos?
faq.a: Yes, presets work with any JPG, PNG or WebP, including smartphone photos. The photo is processed in your browser and the result is downloaded as a JPG.

faq.q: How is a preset different from a social media filter?
faq.a: A preset is a set of exposure, contrast, shadow, color and toning adjustments, just like in Lightroom. You can smoothly change its strength from 0 to 200% and compare the result with the original.

faq.q: Is there a preset for a misty morning?
faq.a: Yes, “Misty Morning”: softer contrast, cool tones and muted colors. You'll find it under the “Overcast” filter.

presetsUrban.title: Presets for city photos and architecture
presetsUrban.text1: City photography loves contrast and clean lines. The “Street” presets add a film-like texture and deeper shadows, so a street looks alive rather than like a flat phone snapshot. “Minimal” mutes colors and brightens the frame, which works well for architecture, concrete, bright interiors and plain backgrounds.
presetsUrban.text2: Teal and orange contrast is a favorite movie trick: warm skin and lights against cool shadows. In a city shot it makes an ordinary street look like a film still. If the colors feel too strong, reduce the effect strength — the preset keeps the mood but becomes subtler.

faq.q: Which preset works for architecture?
faq.a: Choose the “Minimal” filter: “Urban Minimal White” and “Studio Clean” make the frame bright and clean, mute extra colors and emphasize lines.

faq.q: What is the teal and orange style?
faq.a: It's a color scheme where shadows shift toward teal while warm tones (skin, streetlights) stay orange. It gives a cinematic feel and looks great on streets in the evening.

faq.q: Which preset gives street photos a film look?
faq.a: “35mm Street”: stronger contrast, restrained colors, a vignette and visible grain. It's also in the “Film & retro” collection.

faq.q: Are there city presets for evening shots?
faq.a: Yes, “City Lights” and “Cyber Neon / Night” work for both city and night photos. More are in the “Night photos” collection.

presetsNight.title: How to edit a night photo with a preset
presetsNight.text1: Night shots usually have two problems: they're dark and the colors look muddy because of mixed light from streetlamps, signs and headlights. The “City lights” presets separate warm lights from cool shadows, so the shot looks cleaner and moodier. “Neon” boosts the pinks, purples and teals of signs, while “Moody” deepens the shadows for a cinematic image.
presetsNight.text2: If a photo was taken in very weak light and you can barely see anything, start with “Low Light Rescue”. It raises exposure and shadows and mutes blue and purple color noise. It won't create detail out of total darkness, but it often makes the shot usable for viewing and posting.

faq.q: How do I brighten a dark night photo?
faq.a: Choose “Low Light Rescue” and, if needed, raise the effect strength to 130–150%. For dark daytime photos there's a separate “Brighten a dark photo” collection.

faq.q: Why do night photos look noisy?
faq.a: In low light the camera amplifies the signal, which creates colored speckles. A preset won't remove noise completely, but it mutes the most visible color casts so the noise is less distracting.

faq.q: Which preset suits neon signs?
faq.a: Under the “Neon” filter: “Cyber Neon / Night”, “Neon Purple” and “Retro 80s” boost pinks, purples and teals.

faq.q: Which preset suits a car photo at night?
faq.a: “Dark Garage”: deep shadows, muted colors and bright reflections on the body. It's also in the “Cars” collection.

presetsSummer.title: Summer presets for vacation photos
presetsSummer.text1: Summer photos are often overexposed: bright sun blows out the sky and sand, and water loses its color. The presets in this collection tame highlights, lift shadows and bring saturation back to water and sky. “Beach” and “Sea” make the water turquoise, “Sunny” adds warmth and punch, and “Travel” brings out the colors of streets, markets and cities.
presetsSummer.text2: To make a vacation series look consistent on social media, pick one or two presets and apply them to every shot at the same strength. The retro styles “90s Disposable” and “Lomo Pop” recreate the look of a film point-and-shoot — a popular aesthetic for summer stories.

faq.q: How do I make water in a photo turquoise?
faq.a: Choose “Sea Breeze” or “Ocean & Summer” under the “Beach” filter: they boost the turquoise and blue tones of water and sky.

faq.q: What if the sky in my photo is white?
faq.a: These presets tone down the brightest areas, but a completely blown-out sky can't be recovered — there's simply no data left. Shots where the sky still has some color work best.

faq.q: Is there a disposable-camera preset?
faq.a: Yes, “90s Disposable” and “Lomo Pop”: punchy contrast, saturated colors, a vignette and light grain. More styles like these are in the “Film & retro” collection.

faq.q: Which preset suits travel photos of streets and markets?
faq.a: “Bangkok Street” adds warmth and brings out the colors of streets and markets. For bright sunny shots, try “Sunny Pop”.

presetsAuto.title: Presets for automotive photography
presetsAuto.text1: A car looks striking in a photo when you can see the shape of the body: reflections, lines and depth of paint. The “Clean” presets add contrast and highlights without distorting the color — the shot looks like it was taken in a showroom. “Moody” deepens the shadows and leaves only the reflections bright, while “Sunset” gives warm golden tones for rolling shots or road trips.
presetsAuto.text2: Important: if you're photographing a car for a sale listing, stylized presets can hurt — buyers distrust photos where the car's color differs from reality. For that case there's a separate “Car for sale” collection with presets that only brighten and clarify the shot.

faq.q: Which preset should I use for car photos on social media?
faq.a: For a bright magazine look — “Bright Automobile” or “Showroom Gloss”. For moody night shots — “Dark Garage” or “Cinematic Moody”.

faq.q: Are these presets OK for a sale listing?
faq.a: Better use the “Car for sale” collection: its presets don't change the body color, they only brighten the shot and make it sharper-looking.

faq.q: Do presets change the car's color?
faq.a: Stylized presets (such as “Sunset Drive” or “Dark Garage”) change the overall tone of the shot. If you need accurate color, lower the strength or choose a preset from the “Clean” filter.

faq.q: Is there a preset for car photos at sunset?
faq.a: Yes, “Sunset Drive”: warm golden tones and richer reds and oranges. It's under the “Sunset” filter.

presetsAutumn.title: How to make autumn photos more vibrant
presetsAutumn.text1: Fall photos often come out dull: leaves look less vivid than in real life and a gray sky makes the picture flat. The “Golden autumn” presets boost the oranges and reds of the leaves and mute the greens, bringing fall colors to the front. “Crimson Leaves” emphasizes deep reds, while “Autumn Gold” focuses on soft golden light.
presetsAutumn.text2: For photos with coffee, books, blankets and sweaters, try the “Cozy” presets — warm, slightly muted, with soft shadows. For rainy streets and fog there's “Moody”: cooler shadows, deeper contrast and restrained colors. The effect strength can be adjusted smoothly from 0 to 200%.

faq.q: Which preset makes leaves more vivid?
faq.a: “Crimson Leaves” and “Autumn Gold” boost the reds, oranges and yellows of the leaves. If the effect is too weak, raise the strength to 130–150%.

faq.q: Are there cozy presets for coffee or book photos?
faq.a: Yes, the “Cozy” filter: “Cozy Autumn”, “Warm Knit” and “Retro 70s” give warm, muted colors in the style of fall photos on Pinterest.

faq.q: How do I edit a photo from a gloomy fall day?
faq.a: Try the “Moody” filter to emphasize the atmosphere, or the “Nature” collection with the “Overcast” filter to make the shot brighter and more colorful instead.

faq.q: Do the autumn presets work for portraits?
faq.a: Yes. “Golden Hour Glow” gently warms the skin, and “Warm Knit” gives cozy, muted colors for sweater shots. For portraits, 60–80% strength is often enough.

presetsWinter.title: Presets for winter and holiday photos
presetsWinter.text1: The main problem with winter photos is blue or gray snow: the camera mistakenly cools down the white. The “Clean Snow” preset warms the white balance slightly and brightens the frame, so the snow looks white again. If you want to emphasize the frost instead, choose the “Frosty” filter — cool blue shadows and restrained colors.
presetsWinter.text2: For Christmas and New Year photos there are “Festive” presets: they boost reds and golds, make string lights warmer and add a gentle vignette. “Cozy” presets suit home shots by the tree, with cocoa and presents.

faq.q: Why is the snow blue in my photo and how do I fix it?
faq.a: Cameras often get the white balance wrong on snow and make it cold. The “Clean Snow” preset warms the shot a little and brightens the whites, so the snow looks more natural.

faq.q: Which preset works for Christmas photos with string lights?
faq.a: “Holiday Lights” and “Christmas Warm Fireside” under the “Festive” filter: warm lights, rich reds and a soft vignette.

faq.q: Can I make a photo look cold and frosty?
faq.a: Yes, the “Frosty” filter includes “Frosty Blue” and “Misty Morning” — they add cool blue tones and a light haze.

faq.q: What's the difference between “Clean Snow” and “Frosty Blue”?
faq.a: “Clean Snow” warms the white balance slightly and brightens the shot so the snow looks white. “Frosty Blue” does the opposite: it cools the photo and mutes warm colors.

presetsFilm.title: How to add a film effect to a photo online
presetsFilm.text1: Film presets imitate the character of analog photos: softer contrast, lifted blacks, distinctive tints in the shadows and highlights, and light grain. “Analog film” resembles classic color negative stock — warm skin tones and muted greens. “35mm” gives a contrasty street look with visible grain, and “Vintage” recreates the faded colors of old prints.
presetsFilm.text2: Retro presets reproduce the look of each decade: orange-brown 70s, neon-pink 80s and the punchy snapshots of a 90s disposable camera. “Lomo” delivers saturated colors and a heavy vignette, and “Polaroid” soft pastel tones. “Sepia” adds the brown toning of old photographs, and “Noir” the hard black and white contrast of classic cinema. Preset names describe the look, not a specific brand of film.

faq.q: How do I make a photo look like film?
faq.a: Choose a preset under the “Analog film” or “35mm” filter — they soften contrast, lift the blacks, shift shadow colors and add grain. Fine-tune the strength with the slider.

faq.q: Is grain added like on real film?
faq.a: Yes, most film and retro presets add light grain that is most visible in the midtones, just like real film. If there's too much grain, lower the effect strength.

faq.q: Which preset looks like the 90s or a disposable camera?
faq.a: “90s Disposable”: punchy contrast, juicy colors, a slight green tint, a vignette and grain — like a shot from a single-use camera.

faq.q: Are these real Kodak or Fujifilm presets?
faq.a: No, they're our own presets inspired by classic film stocks, with no connection to any manufacturer. They recreate the general character of analog photos rather than the exact curves of a specific film.

faq.q: Can I make sepia or black and white retro photos?
faq.a: Yes, under the “Sepia” and “Noir” filters. “Classic Sepia” gives the brown toning of old photos, while “Film Noir” and “Black & White Moody” give high-contrast black and white.

presetsCinematic.title: Cinematic color grading for photos online
presetsCinematic.text1: Cinematic presets bring movie color-grading techniques to photos. The best known is teal and orange. Shadows shift toward cool teal while skin and lights stay warm, which gives the shot depth and an expensive look. “Moody” relies on deep shadows and muted colors, while “Warm” goes for soft, slightly faded film tones.
presetsCinematic.text2: Black and white cinematic presets suit portraits and street scenes where light and shape matter. Composition helps a photo look like a film still too: a wide frame, a person in profile, side light. The preset completes the effect — and the intensity slider keeps you from overdoing it.

faq.q: What is a cinematic preset?
faq.a: It's a set of color and tone adjustments that imitates film color grading. Typical looks: teal shadows with warm highlights, deep shadows, or muted film colors.

faq.q: Which preset looks most like a movie still?
faq.a: Try “Blockbuster Teal & Orange” or “Urban Cyan & Orange” under the “Teal & orange” filter, and “Cinematic Moody” for a darker mood.

faq.q: Does it work for portraits?
faq.a: Yes, but for portraits it's better to lower the strength to 50–80% so skin stays natural. Dedicated portrait presets are in the “Portrait” collection.

faq.q: Do I need to install Lightroom?
faq.a: No, the presets work right in your browser, with no software and no sign-up.

presetsBrightenDark.title: Why photos come out dark and how to fix them
presetsBrightenDark.text1: A photo usually turns out dark when there's a very bright light source in the frame: a window, the sky or a lamp. The camera lowers exposure so it doesn't blow out, and the face or subject ends up in shadow. Simply raising overall brightness doesn't help — the window and sky turn into white patches. That's why these presets work selectively: they lift shadows and midtones much more and even tone down the highlights a little.
presetsBrightenDark.text2: If the photo was taken in the evening or indoors with poor light, choose “Low Light Rescue” — it brightens more strongly and mutes color noise. For slightly dull daytime shots, “Bright & Clear” is enough. Compare with the before/after slider and adjust the strength from 0 to 200% until the photo looks natural.

faq.q: How do I make a photo brighter without blowing out the highlights?
faq.a: Choose “Brighten Shadows”: it lifts shadows much more than highlights and even tones down the brightest areas slightly, so windows and sky don't burn out.

faq.q: Can a very dark night photo be brightened?
faq.a: Yes, “Low Light Rescue” at 150–200% brightens the shot noticeably. But no filter can recover detail the camera never captured, and noise will become more visible.

faq.q: What if colors look washed out after brightening?
faq.a: Try “Bright & Clear”: it brightens the shot and adds contrast and punch at the same time.

faq.q: Can I brighten only the dark areas?
faq.a: A preset affects the whole frame. But “Brighten Shadows” lifts dark areas much more than bright ones, so the result is close to brightening only the shadows.

presetsProductPhoto.title: How to make product photos appealing to buyers
presetsProductPhoto.text1: For marketplace listings, online stores and Instagram shops, a bright, clean photo with true colors sells better than a dark or yellowish one. Most products are shot at home under lamps, so the picture comes out dark and yellow-tinted. These presets brighten the shot, remove the yellow cast from whites and add clarity to details. The product's own color stays the same.
presetsProductPhoto.text2: A preset doesn't replace the background. If the product was shot on white paper or a white wall, “Clean White Product” makes that background lighter and closer to white. If you need a perfectly white or transparent background, remove it with a separate tool first, then apply a preset for light and color. And remember: the product color in the photo must match reality, otherwise you'll get returns and bad reviews.

faq.q: How do I get a white background on a product photo?
faq.a: The “Clean White Product” preset brightens a light background and removes the yellow cast. For a fully white or transparent background, use the “Remove Background” tool.

faq.q: Will the preset change the product color?
faq.a: The presets in this collection barely change color: they work with light, whites and clarity. Compare before/after and lower the strength if needed.

faq.q: What size will the photo be?
faq.a: The result is saved as a JPG with the long side up to 2000 pixels — enough for listings and product pages. To meet a marketplace file-size limit, use “Compress to a Size”.

faq.q: Which preset suits a product shown in an interior?
faq.a: “Lifestyle Product”: soft warm light for decor, textiles, cosmetics and handmade goods. For a product on a white background, “Clean White Product” works better.

presetsCarSale.title: How to photograph and edit a car for a listing
presetsCarSale.text1: Buyers decide whether to open a listing from the first few photos. Bright shots in soft daylight work best, on a clean background, with visible details: the body from four sides, the interior, the dashboard, the wheels. The presets in this collection improve light and contrast, open up shadows in the interior and emphasize the body's shape — without changing the car's color.
presetsCarSale.text2: Why avoid stylized filters when selling? Buyers are wary of photos where the car's color changes from shot to shot or differs from reality. It looks like an attempt to hide defects. Apply the same preset at the same strength to the whole series, and the listing will look tidy and honest.

faq.q: Which preset should I choose for a car sale listing?
faq.a: Start with “Bright Automobile” — it enhances body reflections and brightens shadows without changing color. For interior shots, “Bright & Clear” works well.

faq.q: What if the photos were taken on a cloudy day?
faq.a: Choose “Overcast Boost”: it adds light and a little warmth, so the car and background don't look gray.

faq.q: Can I use presets from the “Cars” collection?
faq.a: For social media, yes. For listings, avoid stylized presets like “Dark Garage” or “Sunset Drive”: they change the overall tone and the body color.

faq.q: What if the listing site limits the photo file size?
faq.a: Compress the finished photo with the “Compress to a Size” tool: it picks the quality to fit the file size you need.

presetsFood.title: How to edit food photos so they look appetizing
presetsFood.text1: Dishes look tasty in a photo when they have warm, rich colors, visible texture and no blue or green cast from lamps. “Warm Appetizing Food” adds warmth and saturation to reds and oranges — pastries, meat, soups, pizza. “Fresh & Bright Food” brightens the shot and emphasizes fresh greens — for salads, breakfasts, bowls and desserts.
presetsFood.text2: “Moody Food” is a dark restaurant style: deep shadows, a dark background and focus on the dish. It works well for evening menus, bars and photos on dark boards or plates. For a venue's whole menu, stick to one preset — your delivery page or Instagram profile will look consistent.

faq.q: Which preset should I use for menu photos?
faq.a: For most dishes — “Warm Appetizing Food”. For salads and light breakfasts — “Fresh & Bright Food”, for evening menus and bars — “Moody Food”.

faq.q: How do I remove the yellow lamp cast from food photos?
faq.a: Try “Bright & Clear” or “Fresh & Bright Food” — they make the shot brighter and more neutral. If the photo is very yellow, it's better to reshoot it in daylight by a window.

faq.q: Is this good for Instagram?
faq.a: Yes. To keep your feed consistent, apply the same preset at the same strength to all photos.

faq.q: How do I crop a dish photo for Instagram?
faq.a: After applying a preset, use the “Crop Image” tool. It has ready-made ratios, including a 1:1 square and a vertical 3:4.

presetsAvatar.title: What makes a good profile picture
presetsAvatar.text1: People see a profile picture small: in chat lists, comments or search results. So simple things matter: the face is well lit and fills most of the frame, the background is calm and the skin tone looks natural. Heavy filters hurt here. People should recognize you in real life, and for LinkedIn or a résumé over-editing looks unprofessional.
presetsAvatar.text2: That's why this collection contains only subtle presets. “Natural Skin” evens out light and skin tone, and “Studio Clean” gives a neutral business look. “Timeless B&W” makes a restrained black and white portrait. After editing, you can crop the photo into a circle with transparent corners, and the avatar will look good on any background.

faq.q: Which preset should I use for a LinkedIn or résumé photo?
faq.a: “Studio Clean” or “Natural Skin”: they improve light and color without stylizing the photo.

faq.q: How do I make a round avatar?
faq.a: Apply a preset, download the result and crop it into a circle with the “Circle Crop Photo” tool — the corners will be transparent.

faq.q: Can I make a black and white profile picture?
faq.a: Yes, “Timeless B&W” gives a soft classic black and white photo without harsh contrast.

faq.q: Can I remove the background behind me?
faq.a: A preset doesn't change the background. Remove it with the “Remove Background” tool, then crop the photo into a circle.

presetsWedding.title: Wedding presets: how to choose a style
presetsWedding.text1: A wedding shoot means hundreds of frames in different light. There's getting ready indoors, an outdoor ceremony, a sunset walk and an evening at the venue. To make the album consistent, choose one main style. “Bright & Airy Wedding” is the most popular: light, with soft shadows and a clean white dress. “Analog Warm 400” gives a warm film look for atmospheric documentary coverage.
presetsWedding.text2: Black and white shots are a wedding photography classic: “Timeless B&W” conveys emotions well — parents' tears, laughter, hugs — and makes photos timeless. For a sunset walk, try “Golden Hour Glow”. All presets work in your browser: photos aren't uploaded to a server, so your personal shots stay with you.

faq.q: What's the best preset for wedding photos?
faq.a: The most versatile is “Bright & Airy Wedding”. For a warm film style — “Analog Warm 400”, for a classic look — “Timeless B&W”.

faq.q: Can I edit a whole wedding album the same way?
faq.a: A preset is applied to one photo at a time. To keep the album consistent, use the same preset and the same strength for every shot.

faq.q: Is it safe to edit personal photos here?
faq.a: Yes, everything happens in your browser and your photos are never sent anywhere.

faq.q: Do these presets work for engagement or christening photos?
faq.a: Yes, the light, pastel and black and white presets work well for any special or family occasion.

convertMovToMp4.text1: Upload a MOV (QuickTime) video — the format iPhones, iPads and Apple cameras record by default — and get a ready MP4 that opens on virtually any device, platform or video editor.
convertMovToMp4.text2: Conversion runs on a processing server in a few seconds — nothing to install, and no quality loss beyond what's needed for a compatible codec.
convertMovToMp4.dropzone: Drop your MOV file here or click to convert
convertMovToMp4.limit: You've used all your free conversions for today. Sign up to get more!
convertMovToMp4.limit2: You've reached the daily video conversion limit. Please try again tomorrow.

convertMkvToMp4.text1: Upload an MKV (Matroska) video — common for movie rips and recordings with multiple audio/subtitle tracks — and get an MP4 that opens on phones, smart TVs and any player without extra codecs.
convertMkvToMp4.text2: Conversion runs on a processing server in a few seconds — nothing to install. MKV often carries video codecs (HEVC, VP9) that MP4 only partially supports, so the tool re-encodes the video to H.264 for guaranteed compatibility.
convertMkvToMp4.dropzone: Drop your MKV file here or click to convert
convertMkvToMp4.limit: You've used all your free conversions for today. Sign up to get more!
convertMkvToMp4.limit2: You've reached the daily video conversion limit. Please try again tomorrow.

convertWebmToMp4.text1: Upload a WebM video — the format typically used for screen recordings, webcam captures and browser-based recording tools — and get an MP4 that any video editor, presentation app or older platform without WebM support can open.
convertWebmToMp4.text2: Conversion runs on a processing server in a few seconds — nothing to install. WebM and MP4 use different video codecs, so the tool re-encodes the video to H.264, the most widely supported option.
convertWebmToMp4.dropzone: Drop your WebM file here or click to convert

videoToMp3.text2: Everything happens in your browser: the video isn't uploaded anywhere, there's no sign-up and no daily limit.

trimVideo.text1: Cut the part you need out of an MP4, MOV, WebM or MKV file: pick the start and end, preview the clip and save it.
trimVideo.text2: Trimming happens in your browser — the video isn't uploaded to a server, and fast mode doesn't re-encode the file, so quality stays the same.
trimVideo.dropzone: Drop a video here or click to trim it
trimVideo.probing: Your browser can't preview this video — detecting its length…
trimVideo.noPreview: Your browser can't preview this format, but you can still trim it: enter the start and end times.
trimVideo.formatHint: You can type the time as min:sec, e.g. 1:05.5
trimVideo.fastHint: Fast mode: no re-encoding, same quality as the original. The cut snaps to the nearest keyframe, so the start may move a second or two earlier.
trimVideo.preciseHint: Precise mode: the cut lands exactly on your times and the result is an MP4 (H.264). Processing in the browser takes longer, especially on a phone.
trimVideo.noteFast: No re-encoding: same quality as the original.
